Inside the Side-Hustle Economy: What Happened When I Tested Influencer Passive Income Schemes

30 Oct 2026, 11:22 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Business Desk · Source: www.theguardian.com

Key takeawaysSocial media feeds have increasingly featured creators promising thousands of dollars in passive income with minimal effort. Amid global financial pressures and a rising cost of living, millions of users have engaged with hashtags like sidehustle and passiveincome on

Social media feeds have increasingly featured creators promising thousands of dollars in passive income with minimal effort. Amid global financial pressures and a rising cost of living, millions of users have engaged with hashtags like #sidehustle and #passiveincome on platforms such as Instagram and TikTok, searching for flexible ways to supplement their incomes.

To examine the reality behind these claims, an investigative test was conducted over six months across several popular online side hustles, including selling digital templates and engaging in affiliate marketing. The findings reveal that while some individuals do achieve financial success, the promises made by influencers often obscure the substantial labor, marketing skill, and market saturation inherent in these digital ventures.

Testing Digital Templates and Affiliate Marketing

The initial experiment focused on designing and selling digital stationery templates using Canva and listing them on Etsy—a strategy frequently touted by influencers as an easy route to steady revenue. However, the process proved far from effortless. Creating marketable designs required hours of technical formatting, and marketplaces were already heavily saturated with similar products. After dozens of hours of work, initial sales generated minimal revenue, resulting in a net loss once platform fees and subscriptions were factored in.

Subsequent attempts at affiliate marketing yielded similar barriers. Efforts to promote products through personalized links on secondary accounts ran into strict platform policies, low search impressions, and application rejections from major affiliate networks due to insufficient existing web traffic.

Industry Analysis and the 'New Face' of Multilevel Marketing

Experts note that the psychology driving side-hustle culture mirrors historical multilevel marketing (MLM) structures, though without a single corporate hierarchy. Instead of selling physical inventory to friends and family, modern creators often monetize the instructions themselves through masterclasses, ebooks, and online coaching programs.

Communications and economics researchers emphasize that viral side-hustle promotions frequently omit basic economic principles, such as market demand and competition. While a small percentage of participants—often those with prior experience in retail, digital marketing, or specific niches—do build profitable businesses, achieving success generally requires traditional sales expertise, persistent effort, and favorable algorithmic exposure rather than a few minutes of daily work.

Practical Implications and Reader Verification

For readers evaluating online side-hustle claims, experts suggest maintaining realistic expectations regarding income and labor.

  • What is confirmed: Digital marketplaces like Etsy and affiliate platforms are crowded with generic content and AI-generated products, making organic visibility difficult for newcomers.
  • What remains unknown: Exact aggregate failure rates across passive income schemes are hard to quantify, as online spaces rarely highlight unsuccessful attempts.
  • How to verify: Readers can review official platform fee schedules directly on marketplaces like Etsy and consult economic research on digital labor by exploring studies from academic institutions cited in media reports, or by reviewing original reporting at The Guardian.
